task_spec.log_ref: docs/agents/LOGS.md, [2026-09-03] phase-audit workflow + Decimal-precision cost accounting -- spec -> plan -> implementation, no branch/PR yet (Bugs found)
task_spec.description: A gateway config YAML sets `budget_usd: 1` (a bare, unquoted digit) on a virtual key. controlplane.parseYAMLScalar's boolean detection used strconv.ParseBool, which also accepts "0"/"1" as valid booleans -- so `budget_usd: 1` silently parsed as the Go bool `true`, failed the numeric field's type switch, and fell back to the zero value, which budget.Tracker's own convention reads as UNLIMITED budget. A one-digit, typo-free config value could silently disable spend enforcement entirely -- security-relevant (a silent fail-open on a spend cap), not just a display/correctness bug.
task_spec.pre_fix_behavior: budget_usd_parsed=0 (bare digit 1 misread as bool true, numeric type-switch falls through to the zero value) -- budget.Tracker.Allow treats the key as having NO cap at all
task_spec.regression_guard: gateway/internal/gateway/controlplane/config_test.go: TestLoadBudgetUSDBareDigitIsNotMisreadAsBool is the real, executing regression guard for this bug.

task_spec.log_ref: docs/agents/LOGS.md, [2026-09-04] Backlog Phase 2a -- evals rollout cost/DoS mitigation, a naive design corrected before any code shipped (Bugs found)
task_spec.description: evals.rollout.scheduler.run_suite's --use-cache lookup had no defensive check of its own that a matching prior Run (looked up by cache_key in the caller-supplied cached_runs dict) was actually status == "completed" -- it relied solely on rollout_cmd's own cached_runs construction (which filters on status=="completed") to keep an error/timed_out Run out of the cache. Any other caller of run_suite (or a future CLI change) that passed in an error-status Run under its real cache_key would have had run_suite fabricate a fake, silently-reused "completed" hit from what was really a transient infra failure (e.g. the Docker daemon being briefly unreachable), never re-attempting the real sandboxed command.

An early draft always included axis in the canonical JSON dict used to build the SHA-256 hash -- as a literal null when the caller passed axis=None -- which would have silently changed score_cache_key's value for every pre-existing, already-persisted --use-score-cache entry the moment this shipped, breaking every prior cache hit with no warning.
task_spec.pre_fix_behavior: score_cache_key(axis=None)=changed_from_pre_axis_hash (a literal null axis field added to the canonical JSON dict changes the SHA-256 hash for every call that omits axis, invalidating every pre-existing --use-score-cache entry with no warning)
task_spec.regression_guard: evals/tests/test_judge_cache.py::test_omitting_axis_matches_the_original_pre_axis_key_exactly is the real, executing regression guard for this bug.
task_spec.corpus_note: Hand-authored directly into the regression tier per docs/rfcs/2026-09-07-evals-regression-corpus-conventions.md's Phase 3 corpus-growth pass (mined from docs/agents/LOGS.md), not promoted from a real Run+Score via `evals promote` -- stated explicitly, not implied otherwise. Unlike Phase 1's entirely Go-side (gateway) cases, this bug is genuinely evals-side Python (evals.judge.cache.compute_score_cache_key) -- but verified directly, by reading both run_cmd and rollout_cmd in evals/evals/cli.py before concluding this, that neither CLI executor can invoke a cache-key-hashing helper as a per-case task_spec. This case therefore stays in the same static, frozen task_spec.output-vs-reference shape every other case in this file uses, and `evals run` does not re-execute `evals/evals/judge/cache.py` for this case shape at eval time -- it only checks a frozen string. Independently re-confirmed by directly re-running `evals/tests/test_judge_cache.py::test_omitting_axis_matches_the_original_pre_axis_key_exactly` against the real, currently-fixed code before writing this entry (passes), not just quoted from LOGS.md's prose. This case exists for corpus-building and cross-harness visibility of an already-fixed, already-tested bug; it is not a replacement for the real regression guard named above.

reference: score_cache_key(axis=None)=identical_to_pre_axis_hash (axis included in the canonical JSON only when not None)

task_spec.log_ref: docs/agents/LOGS.md, [2026-09-05] Tier 2, final item: real mixture-SPRT (anytime-valid) early-stopping (Bugs found)
task_spec.description: evals.stats.mixture_sprt_early_stop's first draft compared its mSPRT likelihood ratio directly (via math.exp of a log-likelihood term) against 1/alpha, rather than working in log-space throughout. Hypothesis property-based fuzzing (test_never_stops_at_zero_trials_and_never_raises_for_valid_input, run over a broad float/int space) found a real OverflowError on an extreme, previously-unconsidered input -- trials_run=18, successes_frac=1.0, baseline_pass_rate=0.01171875 -- that no hand-picked example test would ever have chosen; the real (non-log) likelihood ratio for this input is astronomically large (its own log-likelihood-ratio is ~717.6, already past what math.exp can represent as a float).
task_spec.pre_fix_behavior: mixture_sprt_decision(trials_run=18, successes=18, baseline_pass_rate=0.01171875)=OverflowError_raised (the raw, non-log likelihood ratio -- math.exp of a log-likelihood-ratio of ~717.6 -- exceeds what a Python float can represent)
task_spec.regression_guard: evals/tests/test_stats_properties.py::test_never_stops_at_zero_trials_and_never_raises_for_valid_input (a Hypothesis property-based fuzz test) is the real, executing regression guard for this bug.
